column1: # gates/held-trees.tsv - THE REGISTER OF GATED-GREEN TREES THAT MUST NOT SHIP.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A "GATES GREEN" log says the gate suite passed over a bundle. It does NOT say that the
# tree shipped, or that it may. At 2026-10-01T00:31Z a run looking for a way out of a deadlock found a
# gated-green ancestor, ran every mechanical check this project provides, got four greens, and pushed a tree
# that #441 had deliberately held. All four checks were correct and none of them could see the hold:
#   git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main e765135          -> true
#   gates/verify-log.sh .../441-all.log '#441'                -> OK (47 suites, 3097 PASS, footer agrees)
#   git show e765135:app.js | md5sum                          -> a4df39c38222, the md5 that log's footer names
#   git show e765135 --stat                                   -> adds only the log file
# The only warning in existence was one sentence in a prose table cell on an unmerged branch: RUN-LOG.md:247 ON
# origin/claude/cool-noether-gccllp, reading "then stood down on two P0s from the adversarial pass" - which no
# tool reads and which main does not even carry. NAME THE TREE WHEN YOU CITE THAT LINE: both of #450's
# antagonists independently called this citation dangling, because line 247 OF MAIN is #437's job-counting rule,
# and the citation is exactly right on the tree where the sentence lives. One line number meaning two different
# things on two trees is not a footnote, it IS the defect.
# The push was reverted 17 minutes later by its own antagonist pass.
# Filed as jobs/a-gated-green-log-is-not-a-shippable-tree-2026-10-01 (P0, priority 11). This file is its fix.
# WHAT MAKES THIS A GUARD AND NOT A NOTE. It is keyed on things a LATER run can compute from the artefact it is
# holding, with no network and no tracker: the BUNDLE MD5 and the GATED SHA. gates.sh writes both into every log
# IT WRITES (the header line carries "md5 <hex>", the ref line carries "ref: HEAD <sha> | bundle md5 <hex>"), and
# `md5sum app.js` recovers the first from any tree on disk.
# BUT NOT INTO EVERY LOG THAT EXISTS, and the first draft of this paragraph said "every log", which antagonist B
# measured and disproved: the ref line arrived at #417, and 52 OF THE 81 COMMITTED GATELOGS (64%) carry no
# `ref: HEAD` line at all. verify-log.sh skips the sha comparison when it is absent, so ON MOST OF THIS
# PROJECT'S LOG CORPUS ONLY THE MD5 ARM FIRES. Said plainly because a guard's coverage is not a detail.
# gates/verify-log.sh reads this file BY DEFAULT and
# REFUSES a log naming a held bundle or a held sha. Nothing here is self-reported by the run that wants to push:
# the row is written by the run that HELD the tree, and read by a different run later. This project has recorded
# six separate defects whose single cause was that the check and the thing being checked were the same object;
# a `shippable` field written by the pushing run would have been the seventh.
# HOW TO WRITE A ROW. `gates/held.sh add <bundleMd5> <gatedSha> <#NNN> <reason...>` - or append by hand. Do it in
# THE SAME step as the stand-down, before the run ends, and commit it to MAIN rather than to the per-run branch:
# #441's own warning was lost precisely because it lived only on a branch that never merged, and a reverted
# commit takes its log with it. A row costs one line and survives a container being reclaimed.
# HOW TO CLEAR A ROW. Do NOT delete it. A tree does not become shippable by being forgotten. Change the first
# field to a `-` prefix (e.g. `-a4df39c38222`), which stops it matching, and append to the reason why it was
# cleared, with the sha that superseded it. The history is the useful part.
# A LIMIT OF THE FIRST TWO KEYS, MEASURED AT #450 RATHER THAN LEFT FOR SOMEONE TO FIND. `gates/build.sh:14`
# builds the stamp as `$N - $(TZ=America/New_York date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') ET` and embeds it with
# `--define:__BUILD__`, so THE BUNDLE MD5 CHANGES ON EVERY REBUILD IN A NEW MINUTE even from byte-identical
# source. Both bundleMd5 and gatedSha therefore identify an ARTEFACT, not a source tree: a run that REBUILDS a
# held source tree and commits it gets a fresh md5 and a fresh sha and matches neither. That is not the failure
# this register was written for - the 00:31Z push took an EXISTING gated-green tree, where both keys match - and
# a rebuild has to earn its own green suite anyway. But it is a real hole, so there is a seventh field:
# sourceMd5, `git show <sha>:chess.jsx | md5sum | cut -c1-12`, which is stamp-independent and survives a
# rebuild. `gates/held.sh check` compares it against the working tree's chess.jsx, and SO DOES `verify-log.sh`,
# via the sha on the log's own ref line. THIS PARAGRAPH FIRST SAID verify-log.sh "CANNOT use it and does not
# try", which antagonist A disproved in the same build: that script already reads the working tree for
# --this-bundle, and `git show <ref sha>:chess.jsx | md5sum` is reachable from the log alone. The false version
# is recorded because A's point was that a wrong sentence here is worse than the gap - it tells the next run not
# to bother. ITS OWN LIMIT, also A's: this is an EXACT-BLOB key, so it catches a straight carry-forward of the
# held source (four commits carry #441's chess.jsx byte-identical) and dies the moment one unrelated character
# changes. No key in this register tracks the DEFECT itself; that needs a predicate, and it is filed as
# jobs/a-held-row-should-carry-a-predicate-not-only-a-hash-2026-10-01.
# sourceMd5 is OPTIONAL - older rows and rows whose sha is unreachable may leave it `-`.
# FORMAT: tab-separated. bundleMd5 (first 12 hex, as gates.sh writes it) | gatedSha, COMMA-SEPARATED - every
# sha that names this tree, not only the gated one | build | heldAt
# (ISO-8601 UTC) | heldBy (runId) | reason (one sentence, the specific thing the suite could not see) |
# sourceMd5 (first 12 hex of chess.jsx at that sha, or `-`).
# bundleMd5

column6: HELD ON AN UNANSWERED QUESTION OF KUNAL'S, NOT ON A RED GATE AND NOT ON A VETO - a different kind of row from the two above, said plainly so a later run does not mistake it for either. This is the #442-#447 pile head, origin/claude/cool-noether-4vmw7f at 004cb86, 19 ahead of main and 22 behind. It carries the win-probability ladder Kunal DID rule on (Desk q-classify-on-winprob, choice labels-and-accuracy, 2026-09-28) plus the two P0 fixes #441 was held for and gates 66 and 67. IT CANNOT SHIP IN EITHER STATE. WITH the #441 mate floor, gates/regress/66-winprob-ladder.js:164 goes red: B1 asserts grade.Blunder.b===0 for the mated player while the floor sends a move that newly forces mate against the mover to classify(Infinity), and in PGN_OPERA Black's 15...Nxd7 allows 16.Qb8+ Nxb8 17.Rd8#, so the floor fires on exactly the move B1 says is not a blunder. WITHOUT the floor it is option (ii) of three Kunal must choose between, which is what #450 pushed as e765135 and had reverted 17 minutes later at 364f700. INSTRUMENT: MEASURED, not derived. gate 66 run from a worktree detached at 004cb86 so gate file, gates/lib.js and app.js all come from this sha; harness printed 'bundle: app.js stamp #442 - 2026-09-30 13:26 ET'; 36 PASS / 1 FAIL on three consecutive runs, identical, the single red being 'FAIL B1 ... blackBlunder:1'. EVERY OTHER ASSERTION IS GREEN, including B3 at 88.9% Black accuracy, so this tree is ONE assertion from green and that assertion is the question itself. Log at claude/agents/gatelogs/453-gate66-single-NOT-A-PUSH-GATE.log, which is a single hand-run gate, emits no GATES GREEN and is refused by verify-log.sh by design. The #442 stamp is not a mismatch: git diff 27fab23 004cb86 -- chess.jsx app.js is empty. NO GATE LOG HAS EVER RUN AGAINST THIS BUNDLE - grep of claude/agents/gatelogs for 0bbc5c85b1df and 004cb86 returns nothing - so unlike the rows above this is not a gated green being withheld; there is no green to withhold. CLEARING THIS ROW NEEDS ONE SENTENCE FROM KUNAL, not a re-gate. THE DECISION IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED AND I SAID OTHERWISE IN THIS ROW FIRST, CORRECTED HERE: jobs/gate-66-b1-and-the-mate-floor-disagree-about-what-the-app-should-print-2026-09-30 (priority 10, created 2026-09-30T17:20Z) carries all three outcomes and their costs, and jobs/the-no-floor-control-is-not-green-and-the-desk-item-promises-kunal-that-it-is-2026-09-30 amends it. Its desk field reads OWED and the Desk still has no such question among its 73, measured 2026-10-01T19:5xZ, so the item has been owed 27 hours. The rebase trap is the one new thing here: jobs/the-442-447-pile-is-blocked-on-one-kunal-decision-and-its-rebase-has-a-clean-merge-trap-2026-10-01. THE gatedSha FIELD OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE [R18]: it read 004cb86f6a9, eleven hex characters that `git cat-file -t` calls 'Not a valid object name', because characters 8-11 are not the real sha's (the true commit is 004cb86d595e4a74be3c5d782cd4a736a28b0238, so d595 was written as f6a9). Found by build #454's antagonist A and re-measured here against the object itself; NOT a shallow-clone artefact, since 004cb86 at seven characters resolves to a commit in the same clone. The HOLD never stopped working, by luck rather than design: held.sh's sha arm compares only the first seven characters, so the row still matched. But the value a reader would resolve was unresolvable, which is the whole premise of a register a later run trusts without having written it.

HELD ON AN UPHELD ANTAGONIST VETO, AND THE SUITE NEVER FINISHED. The grading is arithmetically wrong in a way no gate in this suite can see: gradeDrillMove compares a DEPTH-2 score of the played move against a baseline that is the DEPTH-16 stored move, and loss=Math.min(1500,Math.max(0,...)) clamps a NEGATIVE difference to 0, so every move the shallow search happens to rate above the deep baseline is graded Best and told 'Nothing in the position beats it' - antagonist B measured 26 of 33 legal moves accepted in one quiet middlegame, 19 of them only because of that clamp. The mirror case is the same clamp at the ceiling: when the stored move is a mate, vBest is a mate score so every non-mating move reads loss 1500 and Blunder, measured 41 of 42 legal moves with 26 sharing one sentence - and drill cards are captured ONLY for Mistake, Blunder and Miss, so a decisive best move is the feature's normal case and not an edge. This is a WORSE version of the complaint the build was written to fix (Kunal: 'there can only be one best move'). Gate 52 is green at 20 PASS and cannot see any of it, because its fixture is one position with one hanging queen and three inputs. Separately two of the three sentences the feature is built around are unreachable by arithmetic against DRILL_MSG_MAXW=48 - 'Can you find it?' is selected 0 times out of 5 SANs - and my own unit control could not see it because it tested whether any candidate EXCEEDED the budget rather than which candidate was SELECTED. DO NOT SHIP THIS TREE. The grading needs a single instrument on both sides of the comparison before any of it is worth re-gating; see jobs/456-drill-grading-held-on-a-clamped-cross-instrument-loss-2026-10-02. (THE gatedSha IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG FOR ABOUT A MINUTE AND IS CORRECTED HERE BEFORE IT WAS COMMITTED: the first write padded the short hash 8dab924 into a 40-character string I INVENTED rather than reading git rev-parse. A register keyed on a sha is worthless if the sha is fabricated, and it would have failed silently - every later lookup would simply never match. Caught by re-reading my own command. [R18]) ### THREE MORE GROUNDS, FROM THE SECOND ANTAGONIST, EACH ALSO INVISIBLE TO THIS SUITE. (a) AN ACCEPT DESTROYS THE PLAYER'S OWN CARD, IRREVERSIBLY, ON A DEPTH-2 VERDICT: the useEffect keyed on puzSolved filters the card out of ct_mymistakes, and before #456 the only way to reach it was to play the engine's own move. Antagonist A measured 7 moves in one Sicilian middlegame accepted as Excellent at shallow loss 20-35 that a depth-4 ranking puts at 95-135cp. The old failure was "try again", annoying and recoverable; this one deletes captured data. (b) drillAcceptMsg IS NOT BUDGETED AT ALL, in the same 74px box this file budgets twice: measured against #426's own capacity figures for that box, the Excellent branch is 64-68 chars against 61 at 320x568 and the Brilliant branch 63-75, over at 320x568 by 2-14 and over KUNAL'S OWN 375x730 by up to 6 - and the Brilliant branch prefixes p.explain, which mistakeWhy has ALREADY packed to its own 52-char ceiling for this very box. No gate drives Excellent, Good or Brilliant, so C7 and C7b cannot see any of it. (c) C4, THE GATE'S OWN ANTI-GENERIC-STRING ASSERTION, IS FALSE IN THE COMMONEST CARD STATE: on a card whose stored move MATES - "you missed the mate" - vBest is a mate score so every non-mating move clamps to Blunder while bandAfter reads the position honestly, giving "Blunder: leaves you winning", a sentence that contradicts itself, and three different moves give 1 DISTINCT OF 3 after C4's own mask. AND THE BRILLIANT DRILL IS REACHED BY THE GRADING AND SHOULD NOT BE: a different move that gates Brilliant is told "That's your brilliant move. Nicely done." about a move that was not theirs. BOTH ANTAGONISTS ALSO RECORD THAT I REBUILT app.js TWICE WHILE THEY WERE MEASURING, which is the #441 mistake repeated and is why neither pass can be cited against one artefact without checking its timestamps.

column6: HELD ON AN UPHELD ANTAGONIST VETO AND A RED SUITE, and the two are unrelated. (1) THE VETO, from antagonist A at the diff door, re-measured independently by this run before upholding it: DRILL_MSG_MAXW=48 eats the LEAD CANDIDATE of all three branches of drillAcceptMsg, so "Best move. Nothing in the position beats it." - the headline string named in chess.jsx, in gate 17s header, in US-R14 and in this builds own commit message - CAN NEVER REACH THE SCREEN for any legal SAN; with the apps own emoji prefix the three lead candidates measure 50, 52 and 62 characters against the 48 budget, and the selected string is always candidate 2. Gate 17s A6a/A6b are green BECAUSE those candidates are dead, so they cannot tell "the budget works" from "the budget eats the top of every ladder" - which is the EXACT wrong-shaped control the #456 row was held for, re-created on the accept ladder by the same build that fixed it on the reject ladder. (2) THE GOOD BAND COLLAPSES TO ONE SENTENCE: drillGradeMsgs Good branch reads only the SAN - it never reads bandAfter and never reads takenBack, because the takenBack branch is tested AFTER Good - so 9 bands x 2 takenBack x one SAN yields 1 distinct sentence, measured by this run directly. 49 of gate 17s own 279 graded moves (17.6%, antagonist As count) land in that band with nothing asserted over any of them, so a quiet pawn push leaving you clearly better and a piece hanging that is taken straight back get the identical sentence. That is R10 item 5, for the one band Kunal wrote the words for, in a build whose comments cite R10 item 5 three times as the thing it fixes. THIS ALSO WITHDRAWS THIS BUILDS OWN A6d FIGURE: "180 of 180" counts two loop variables the Good branch cannot read; the honest scope is 1 template over 10 SANs. (3) FOUR MORE GROUNDS FROM THE SAME PASS, each invisible to this suite: the ACCEPT band is unbounded by any assertion and accepts 36.7% and 42.9% of legal moves in two Black-to-move fixtures, which is the #456 rows ground (a) still live in another form; onlineSolved still fires on a graded accept while this builds own ground-2 fix now RETAINS the card, so the same equal-but-not-stored move banks streak and XP without bound on every revisit - a regression this build introduced; mateBaseline uses Math.abs(vBest)>=90000 and is therefore FRAME-BLIND, flagging a position where the mate belongs to the OPPONENT (latent, not shipped, because every move there is loss 0 and takes the accept branch); and a terminal DRAW prints "Blunder: leaves you level. Try again." in a position that no longer exists, the same band-versus-consequence contradiction mateBaseline was added for, one row down. (4) THE RED IS SEPARATE AND IS NOT THIS TREES DEFECT: gate 33 went red on three assertions all reading null because its locator regex uses \w+, which cannot match the legal minified identifier $. origin/mains bundle minifies that slot to X and matches; this bundle minifies it to $ and does not. The apps values are byte-identical in both - guard 2e4 and depth 16 - proven two-sidedly. Fixed in gates/regress/33-reproducible-review.js and pushed to main separately from this tree. DO NOT SHIP THIS BUNDLE. The one-instrument baseline, the card-delete guard, the brilliant-drill exclusion and the mate sentence are all sound and worth keeping; what is owed is the two ladders and the accept band. See jobs/457-drill-sentence-ladders-eat-their-own-lead-candidate-2026-10-02.
